prompt.context_jp: 富士山のふもと、富士浅田市の朝は、いつもと変わらぬ静けさから始まる。
prompt.prompt_jp: 富士浅田市の朝___、いつもと変わらぬ静けさから始まる。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that frames 'the morning in Fujiasada City' as the topic of this opening narration.

feedback.correct_en: This is a scene-setting opening line that presents 'the morning' as the topic the sentence will describe. は signals 'as for the morning here...', which fits an establishing shot.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would announce the morning as brand-new information worth pointing out, as if the listener didn't know a morning existed — too marked for a general scene-setter.

contrast_examples.en: This town (as a topic) is quiet.
Oh, morning has come! (newly noticed event)

prompt.context_jp: チェックアウトの列が絶え、フロントの空気がふと緩んだ。
prompt.prompt_jp: チェックアウトの列___絶え、フロントの空気がふと緩んだ。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that reports the line disappearing as a fresh observed event.

feedback.correct_en: The narrator is describing a change the reader hasn't been tracking yet — the line coming to an end is new, observed information, which takes が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would present 'the line' as an already-established topic being contrasted or commented on, but the sentence is reporting a momentary event, not commenting on the line itself.

contrast_examples.en: The rain stopped. (noticed event — が)
This line is long, isn't it. (comment on topic — は)

prompt.context_jp: 忙しい朝は、こまごました手続きに埋もれがちだが、この時間帯こそフロント係の腕の見せどころだった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 忙しい朝___、こまごました手続きに埋もれがちだ。
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the particle for a generalizing remark 'busy mornings tend to...'.

feedback.correct_en: This is a generic statement about busy mornings as a topic/category. は sets up 'as for busy mornings' and the predicate characterizes them.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would make 'busy mornings' sound like newly-noticed specific information, clashing with the general observation being made.

contrast_examples.en: On holidays (topic), there are a lot of people.
A day off has arrived! (new event)

prompt.context_jp: 次の客がまだ現れず、フロントには由美と奥田だけが残された。
prompt.prompt_jp: フロントには由美と奥田だけ___残された。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits an exhaustive 'only Yumi and Okuda — and nobody else'?

feedback.correct_en: だけ+が emphasizes the exhaustive identification: of everyone, it was precisely these two who remained. が highlights who/what the subject is.
feedback.incorrect_en: だけは would shift to contrast ('at least those two didn't leave, but...'), implying some other comparison not present here.

contrast_examples.en: Only I know (exhaustive).
I alone don't know (contrastive).

prompt.context_jp: 由美の目が伝票の一行で止まり、内心の記録更新が音もなく途切れる。
prompt.prompt_jp: 由美の目___伝票の一行で止まり、内心の記録更新が音もなく途切れる。
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the particle for the sudden, newly-observed action 'her eyes stopped'.

feedback.correct_en: The narrator is zooming in on a fresh event — her eyes stopping. が marks this as new, in-the-moment information for the reader.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would turn 'Yumi's eyes' into a known topic being commented on in general, losing the sense of a sudden, specific moment.

contrast_examples.en: The phone rang. (sudden event)

contrast_examples.jp: 電話はテーブルの上にある。
contrast_examples.en: The phone (as topic) is on the table.

prompt.context_jp: ポケットの中で、清美のスマホが小さく震えた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 清美のスマホ___小さく震えた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that announces the phone's vibration as a new event the reader just witnesses.

feedback.correct_en: The phone vibrating is a sudden event introduced into the scene — classic 'new information' usage of が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would be used if we were already talking about her phone and now commenting on it; here the phone appears as a fresh happening.

contrast_examples.en: The phone buzzed. (new event)
That phone is old. (describing a known topic)

prompt.context_jp: その背中は、噂の小野寺くんに負けず劣らずの速さだった。
prompt.prompt_jp: その背中___、噂の小野寺くんに負けず劣らずの速さだった。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle: the sentence comments on 'that back' which was just introduced.

feedback.correct_en: The previous sentence already brought 'his retreating back' into focus; this sentence makes a comment about that known referent — perfect for は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would re-introduce the back as new information, awkwardly ignoring that the reader just saw it in the prior line.

contrast_examples.en: His retreating figure was fast. (commenting on known subject)
Suddenly a back came into view. (new entity)

prompt.context_jp: それが単なるくつろぎではなく、彼の体力を回復させる大事な儀式であることを知っているのは、清美だけだった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 知っているの___、清美だけだった。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits a cleft 'the one who knew was only Kiyomi'?

feedback.correct_en: In a 「〜のは Xだ」 cleft, は presents the nominalized relative as the topic and X as the exhaustive identification. This is the natural pattern here.
feedback.incorrect_en: 〜のが…だった is possible in some clefts, but 'knew-NOM が Kiyomi dake datta' sounds unidiomatic; the standard focus-cleft here uses は.

contrast_examples.jp: 来たのは田中さんだけだった。
contrast_examples.en: The one who came was only Tanaka.
Tanaka came. (plain new-info statement)

prompt.context_jp: 早く帰る同僚の話が、なぜか高橋の宇宙人説へと繋がりかけたことを、彼女はまだ黙っていられなかった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 彼女___まだ黙っていられなかった。
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the particle: Kiyomi has been the ongoing topic in this paragraph.

feedback.correct_en: Kiyomi is the established topic in this scene; a continuing comment about her uses は for topic continuation.
feedback.incorrect_en: 彼女が would single her out as new/exhaustive subject, as if just now identifying who couldn't stay quiet — out of place when she's clearly the ongoing POV character.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼女はまだ怒っていた。
contrast_examples.en: She was still angry. (continuing topic)
She's the one who got angry! (news/focus)

prompt.context_jp: 窓際のテーブルには、清美と葉月美波、そして葉月の三人組がすでに揃っている。
prompt.prompt_jp: 窓際のテーブルには、清美と葉月美波、そして葉月の三人組___すでに揃っている。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle introduces who is already at the window table?

feedback.correct_en: The 「〜には Xが〜ている」 existential/presentational pattern uses が to point out X existing at the location — classic new-info usage.
feedback.incorrect_en: は after 三人組 would turn them into a topic, but the sentence establishes their location/presence as new scene information. Also, には already marks the topical frame.

contrast_examples.en: There's a cat in the garden. (existence)
That cat is brown. (comment on known topic)

prompt.context_jp: 高橋は視線を宙に泳がせ、遠い記憶を引き出すように少し口を開いた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 高橋___視線を宙に泳がせ、遠い記憶を引き出すように少し口を開いた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle: Takahashi is the ongoing topic of this conversation scene.

feedback.correct_en: Takahashi has been the center of the conversation; は continues him as topic and the predicate describes what he does.
feedback.incorrect_en: 高橋が would spotlight him as newly identified subject, as if the reader didn't know who was speaking — but he's already in focus.

contrast_examples.en: He silently thought. (known topic)
There, he appeared. (new entity)

prompt.context_jp: みなぷーの声が高くなり、店内の視線がわずかにテーブルへ集まった。
prompt.prompt_jp: みなぷーの声___高くなり、店内の視線がわずかにテーブルへ集まった。
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the particle that reports Minapu's voice rising as a sudden event.

feedback.correct_en: A change-of-state description noticed in the moment ('her voice got loud') is prototypical が territory.
feedback.incorrect_en: みなぷーの声は高くなり would read as a general characterization of her voice rather than a one-time, in-scene event.

contrast_examples.en: Her voice got loud. (noticed change)
Her voice is loud. (habitual trait)

prompt.context_jp: 高橋がフィルムに集中する横で、店の入口の自動ドアが柔らかく開いた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 店の入口の自動ドア___柔らかく開いた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits announcing the door opening — a new event just introduced into the scene?

feedback.correct_en: The door opening is a fresh in-scene event that triggers the next action (Ayanyan entering). が introduces it as new information.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would require the door to already be a topic of discussion; here the door simply appears as part of a new happening.

contrast_examples.en: The door opened. (sudden event)
This door is heavy. (describing a known topic)

prompt.context_jp: 客を見送った由美の肩から、ほんのわずかに力が抜けた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 由美の肩から、ほんのわずかに力___抜けた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for the idiomatic '力が抜ける' (strength drains out).

feedback.correct_en: 力が抜ける is a fixed collocation describing an involuntary change — tension leaves her shoulders. が is standard with such spontaneous events.
feedback.incorrect_en: 力は抜けた would set up a contrast ('the strength did drain, but...'), which the narrator isn't making here.

contrast_examples.en: The tension left my shoulders.

contrast_examples.jp: 力は抜けたが、まだ緊張している。
contrast_examples.en: The strength did go out, but I'm still tense. (contrastive)

prompt.context_jp: 客の背中がドアの向こうへ消えると、清美は伝票をそっと束ね直した。
prompt.prompt_jp: 客の背中___ドアの向こうへ消えると、清美は伝票をそっと束ね直した。
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the particle inside this subordinate clause describing the customer leaving.

feedback.correct_en: In 〜と subordinate clauses describing an event-triggering condition, the subject takes が. The main-clause topic (清美は) handles the は role.
feedback.incorrect_en: は inside a 〜と clause would be unusual and would wrongly try to topicalize 'the customer's back' when the real topic of the sentence is Kiyomi.

contrast_examples.jp: ドアが開くと、彼は入ってきた。
contrast_examples.en: When the door opened, he came in.

contrast_examples.jp: ドアは開くが、彼は来ない。
contrast_examples.en: The door opens, but he doesn't come. (contrast)

prompt.context_jp: 「精算お済みですので チェックアウトは以上です いってらっしゃいませ」
prompt.prompt_jp: 精算___ですので、チェックアウトは以上です。
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the polite form that fits this hotel front-desk collocation.

feedback.correct_en: 「精算お済みです」 is the set polite phrase hotel staff use to confirm payment is complete. お+Vます stem+です is a standard respectful construction.
feedback.incorrect_en: 「終わり」 is too casual for guest-facing speech, and 「完了」 is used in writing/announcements, not spoken check-out lines.

contrast_examples.jp: ご予約はお済みでしょうか。
contrast_examples.en: Have you completed your reservation?
I finished my homework. (casual, non-service)

prompt.context_jp: 「ちなみに 今 精算ゼロ 連続17人 更新中です」
prompt.prompt_jp: 精算ゼロ、連続17人、___中です。
prompt.prompt_en: Which word fits 'currently setting a new record'?

feedback.correct_en: 記録を更新する = 'to update/break a record'. 「更新中」 fits the running-tally feeling perfectly.
feedback.incorrect_en: 「変更」 means 'change/modify' (plan, settings) and 「交換」 means 'exchange' — neither works for 'breaking a record'.

contrast_examples.en: Broke the world record.
Changed the schedule.

prompt.context_jp: 「ただの運でしかないので ねらいようがない」
prompt.prompt_jp: ただの___でしかないので、ねらいようがない。
prompt.prompt_en: Which word captures that it's just chance?

feedback.correct_en: 運 = 'luck/chance' — perfectly matches the point that you can't aim for a lucky streak.
feedback.incorrect_en: 縁 means 'fate/connection between people', and 勘 means 'intuition' — neither captures random chance.

contrast_examples.en: That's just luck.
I have a connection with him.

prompt.context_jp: 「途絶えちゃった」
prompt.prompt_jp: ___ちゃった。(連続記録が止まったとき)
prompt.prompt_en: Which verb best describes 'the streak was broken'?

feedback.correct_en: 途絶える specifically means 'a continuing thing is cut off/interrupted' — perfect for a streak coming to an abrupt end.
feedback.incorrect_en: 終わる is just 'end' (not emphasizing interruption of continuity) and 止まる means 'come to a stop' (motion), both weaker here.

contrast_examples.en: Communication was cut off.
The movie ended.

prompt.context_jp: 高橋の秘密を知って以来、集まる口実は前より軽くなり、予定はどこか自然に増えていく。
prompt.prompt_jp: 集まる___は前より軽くなり、予定はどこか自然に増えていく。
prompt.prompt_en: What word means 'excuse / pretext' to get together?

feedback.correct_en: 口実 nuances 'a pretext — a surface reason you give to justify doing what you actually wanted anyway'. Fits the friends inventing reasons to meet.
feedback.incorrect_en: 理由 is a plain 'reason' and 原因 means 'cause (of a problem)' — neither carries the playful 'pretext' nuance the sentence wants.

contrast_examples.en: Look for an excuse to have drinks.
State the reason for absence.

prompt.context_jp: 高橋は覚悟を決めたようにため息をつき、フィルムの角を指の腹でそっと持ち上げた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 高橋は___を決めたようにため息をつき…
prompt.prompt_en: Which noun collocates with 決める to mean 'brace oneself / resolve'?

feedback.correct_en: 覚悟を決める is the fixed collocation for 'to steel oneself / accept what's coming'. Fits Takahashi's resigned sigh.
feedback.incorrect_en: 決意 pairs with 固める/する, not 決める (and 決意を決める is redundant). 気合を入れる would be the match for 'fire oneself up', a different nuance.

contrast_examples.en: Resolve oneself and face it.
Fire up and run.

prompt.context_jp: 本人は毎回“行けたら行く”と口では言うのに、蓋を開ければ、こうして毎回顔を出しているのだった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 本人は毎回“行けたら行く”と口では言うのに、___を開ければ、こうして毎回顔を出している。
prompt.prompt_en: Complete the idiom meaning 'when you actually look at the result...'.

feedback.correct_en: 蓋を開ける(開けてみる) is a set idiom meaning 'once the actual results are revealed'. It fits the contrast with what he says vs. what actually happens.
feedback.incorrect_en: 幕を開ける means 'raise the curtain / start a performance' (beginning, not revelation); 扉 isn't idiomatic in this phrase.

contrast_examples.jp: 蓋を開けてみれば大成功だった。
contrast_examples.en: When all was said and done, it was a huge success.
Open the curtain on a new era.

prompt.context_jp: 「“行けたら行く”は 大抵 来ないときに言うセリフだけど」
prompt.prompt_jp: “___ら行く”は、大抵 来ないときに言うセリフだけど。
prompt.prompt_en: Fill in the conditional form that creates this famously non-committal phrase.

feedback.correct_en: 行けたら = potential-form + たら ('if I can manage to go'). The idiom 行けたら行く hedges on ability, which is why it reads as noncommittal.
feedback.incorrect_en: 行ったら would mean 'if/once I go' (presupposing you will), and 行くなら shifts the sense; neither matches the hedging social script.

contrast_examples.en: I'll come if I have time. (similar hedge)
Let me know once you go.

prompt.context_jp: 由美の返しとして自然に響くのは？
prompt.prompt_en: Yumi has just been told 'let's aim for 20!' Which reply sounds most natural as a dry, Yumi-style comeback?

choices.text: ただの運でしかないので、ねらいようがない。
ただの運だけなので、ねらう方法はありません。
運しかないから、ねらうのが無理です。

feedback.correct_en: 〜でしかない (just/nothing but) + 〜ようがない (there's no way to…) is a crisp, idiomatic pairing that gives Yumi's deadpan tone.
feedback.incorrect_en: Option b is grammatical but sounds like a textbook paraphrase, lacking the idiomatic punch. Option c mixes casual and polite endings awkwardly.

contrast_examples.en: It's nothing more than coincidence.
There's no way to answer.

prompt.context_jp: みなぷーのこだわりへのツッコミとして自然なのは？
prompt.prompt_en: Hatchi teases Minapu for fussing over something minor. Which phrasing sounds most natural?

choices.text: みなぷーって、変なとこ気ぃ遣うよね。
みなぷーって、変な所に気を使っているよね。
みなぷーって、おかしい部分に注意を払うよね。

feedback.correct_en: 変なとこ気ぃ遣う is colloquial speech: contracted 気ぃ, dropped particle, and 変なとこ for '(odd) small details'. It fits the casual chat between friends.
feedback.incorrect_en: Option b is grammatically fine but overly stiff for casual banter. Option c uses 注意を払う (formal/written), which clashes with the register.

contrast_examples.jp: 変なとこ気ぃ遣うなあ。
contrast_examples.en: You stress about the weirdest things.

contrast_examples.jp: 細部に注意を払う必要がある。
contrast_examples.en: One must pay attention to details. (formal)

prompt.context_jp: 手で押さえる動作の『アピール感』を言い表すのに自然なのは？
prompt.prompt_en: Hatchi wants to describe the dramatic 'I'm on the line for you!' vibe of holding the elevator by hand. Which option sounds most natural?

choices.text: “私のことはいいから早く！” みたいな
“私についてはいいので、早くしてください！” みたいな
“私のことは大丈夫、早くね！” みたいな

feedback.correct_en: 「私のことはいいから早く！」 is the natural self-sacrificing line — short, imperative, dramatic. Matches the hammy register being parodied.
feedback.incorrect_en: Option b is way too polite/stiff for a quoted dramatic ad-lib. Option c softens the urgency with 大丈夫・ね, killing the melodrama.

contrast_examples.jp: 俺のことはいいから、先に行け！
contrast_examples.en: Don't worry about me, go on ahead!

contrast_examples.jp: 私については問題ありません。
contrast_examples.en: As for me, there's no issue. (formal, no drama)

prompt.context_jp: 軽い誘いへの返事として、高橋らしく自然なのは？
prompt.prompt_en: Yumi casually invites Takahashi to lunch. Which reply fits his breezy, non-committal register best?

choices.text: う～ん まあ… 行けたら行くわ
もし可能であれば参加させていただきます
行くか行かないか、まだ分かりません

feedback.correct_en: 「行けたら行くわ」 is the classic casual hedge among friends/coworkers — vague on purpose, with sentence-final わ for a relaxed male tone.
feedback.incorrect_en: Option b jumps to keigo, way too formal for coworker banter. Option c is grammatical but awkwardly literal, lacking the easy social script.

contrast_examples.jp: じゃあ行けたら行くね。
contrast_examples.en: Then I'll come if I can. (casual)

contrast_examples.jp: 可能であれば参加いたします。
contrast_examples.en: I'll attend if possible. (business formal)

prompt.context_jp: 貼ったフィルムの完成度を褒めるのに、話し言葉で自然なのは？
prompt.prompt_en: The friends admire the perfectly applied screen protector. Which line sounds most natural as a spoken compliment?

choices.text: 気泡 全然ないじゃん
気泡がまったく存在していない
気泡は一つも見えない状況だ

feedback.correct_en: Dropped が, 全然+negative, and sentence-final じゃん give a lively casual observation among friends — exactly the scene's tone.
feedback.incorrect_en: Option b sounds like a technical report; option c is a stiff descriptive statement. Neither matches excited peer-to-peer speech.

contrast_examples.en: There are no wrinkles at all!

contrast_examples.jp: シワは一切存在しない。
contrast_examples.en: There exist no wrinkles whatsoever. (written/formal)
